items.title: Backend Architecture & High Concurrency
items.description: Designed the microservice architecture for a gaming and live-streaming platform, splitting each game format into its own API, Socket, business service, and async consumer so each scales independently by load. Kafka carries cross-service event streams, Redis and Bull Queue handle caching and async settlement, Socket.IO delivers live rounds and draw results.

items.title: Performance Tuning & Refactoring
items.description: Measures before tuning rather than guessing. One typical case: replacing runtime JSON parsing with virtual generated columns and composite indexes, taking the query from 5s to milliseconds; another traced a connection-count alert to pinned connections left by frozen Lambda containers, where reclaim and retry changes cut peak connections by 24%. Regular scope covers MySQL index and query-plan tuning, Redis cache design, and refactoring legacy code into layered modules.

items.title: Node.js / React.js
items.description: Node.js / NestJS on the backend, React / Next.js (App Router) on the frontend, TypeScript across both — delivering independently from database and API through to the interface. Frontend performance sits in the same scope: first paint, code splitting, caching strategy. Mobile experience includes Flutter.

items.title: Self-Built RAG and Evaluation Framework
items.description: Built a RAG framework from scratch in Python (FastAPI), no LangChain, to keep full control over retrieval strategy and failure degradation: hybrid retrieval with RRF fusion, LLM reranking, two-tier caching, circuit breakers, provider failover. Evaluation uses a golden dataset and LLM-as-a-Judge, with Recall, MRR, and Groundedness running in CI.

items.title: Commercializing AI Features
items.description: Treats LLMs as revenue-bearing features, not demos. Match suggestions, chat coaching, icebreakers, and bio generation were all built on Claude and shipped as paid subscriptions, with cost control, graceful degradation, and content moderation designed in from the start. Claude Code in the development process delivered ten-plus features in one month while two product lines stayed live.

items.title: Team Leadership & Development Standards
items.description: Leading the team shifted the focus from writing code to building repeatable standards: design review to settle architecture before work starts, code review to hold implementation quality, and a release checklist that turns deployment risk from individual experience into process. Troubleshooting was standardized and documented so problem isolation no longer depends on specific people.
